title: China-to-Senegal Lithium Battery & Power Bank Compliance
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: Senegal standards and customs entry governance
rows.target_requirement: Senegal applies import checks through ASN-guided standards references and Ministry of Trade PEC/VoC flow controls. Market access is importer-led and often processed via Dakar port customs channels.
target_standards: ASN standards references and NS/IEC adoption
rows.china_equivalent: China uses GB/GB-T based domestic rules and CCC where applicable. These are important for Chinese domestic compliance but do not represent the full Senegal entry mechanism.
rows.gap: There is no direct single battery law equivalent in this lane. CN certificates are baseline evidence only; Senegal still requires importer-level mapping to PEC/ASN. Senegal does not show EU-style horizontal RoHS or battery passport regimes here.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory practical check via PEC/VoC and importer-led controls for regulated products.
mandatory_status.cn: CN domestic compliance is mandatory domestically, not structurally equivalent to Senegal release obligations

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] CNGB/CCC helps engineering baseline, but importer-led ASN/PEC processing and French documentation are the decisive compliance points for Senegal.

source.publisher: ASN and Senegal Ministry of Trade

rows.target_requirement: Import clearance for lithium batteries and power banks in Senegal requires safety evidence acceptable to local review, aligned with ASN technical expectations and importer-prepared documentation.
target_standards: ASN/NS technical references for battery goods
rows.china_equivalent: China uses GB 31241-2022 and GB 18287-2013 as domestic baselines for safety declarations. These are useful, but need localization for Senegal import evidence.
rows.gap: The practical gap is process and localization, not absence of testing. CN evidence should be adapted for Senegal acceptance, and power system parameters should reflect Senegal's 230 V, 50 Hz baseline.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory when Senegal clearance asks for technical evidence through importer channels.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory within China for domestic applicability

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Use CNGB/GB-T as baseline data, then map and translate for PEC/ASN review. The gap is mainly local process fitness, not test principle itself.

rows.requirement: EMC and radio compliance for power banks
rows.target_requirement: Portable power banks with electronics or wireless features are reviewed for EMC and radio expectations in Senegal, especially for ARTP-relevant goods.
target_standards: ASN technical expectations for electronic products
rows.china_equivalent: China uses GB/T EMC and MIIT/SRRC controls domestically. These are helpful references but do not automatically satisfy Senegal import inspection pathways.
rows.gap: There is no one-to-one EU-style horizontal substance regime in this lane. The gap is mainly importer-ready documentation, French language readiness, and ARTP-facing review alignment.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for imports with relevant radio or electronic compliance review requirements.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory domestically where Chinese rules apply

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] CN approvals are useful but not sufficient; build importer-led French packages and verify ARTP relevance in Senegal before export.

rows.requirement: Market access controls: importer and PEC/VoC
rows.target_requirement: In this lane, Senegal market access is importer-led through PEC and VoC channels, with ASN-aligned technical expectations and French regulatory packets.
rows.china_equivalent: China has domestic filing and certification mechanisms, but these are not the same as the Senegal importer-centered route used here.
rows.gap: The practical gap is governance and documentation. CN paperwork alone is not enough for Senegal release; importer accountability and French documentation are required. No EU-like horizontal EPR/WEEE framework is evidenced in this path.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory practical route: importer-led PEC/VoC compliance and local channel management.
mandatory_status.cn: Not equivalent to Senegal importer-led controls

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Treat importer readiness, PEC/VoC flow, and ASN-linked evidence as primary. CN compliance is a baseline and should be localized for Senegal.

rows.target_requirement: UN 38.3 is required for lithium batteries, battery packs and power banks. For Senegal shipments, align these results with Dakar logistics controls and importer handover requirements.
rows.china_equivalent: China applies UN 38.3 and domestic dangerous-goods frameworks for export. This is necessary baseline support but does not fully replace Senegal arrival-side logistics control.
rows.gap: Transport test standards are largely aligned. The gap is destination-side documentation and process fit, including French packets, Dakar point handling, and onward local transfer. Senegal has no direct EU-like horizontal regime reflected in transport checks here.

mandatory_status.target: UN 38.3 mandatory for international movement and Senegal route handling is mandatory in local chain.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory in Chinese export logistics where applicable

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Keep UN 38.3 records valid and map them to Senegal route controls. Practical compliance is mostly destination documentation and importer coordination.
